To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hyaluronan has a simple repeating disacccharide sequence that is the same in tissues and fluids from all vertebrates, but its average molecular mass varies from tissue to tissue and is increased in inflammatory or remodeling processes.

hyaluronan, a ubiquitous glycosaminoglycan in vertebrates, is synthesized as a polymer with an average molecular weight of about 1,000,000 Da, which can be degraded to fragments that are biologically active.
the size of hyaluronans in biological fluids and in tissues is highly variable and is regulated in response to physiological stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of hyaluronans in the body.
the role of hyaluronans in the regulation of the extracellular matrix and the control of cell behavior in health and disease.
hyaluronan, a ubiquitous extracellular matrix glycosaminoglycan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hyaluronan concentration is generally higher in pathological conditions, and that the hyaluronic acid concentration is higher in the extracellular matrix of tumors compared to normal tissue.
hyaluronan concentration and size distribution are not fixed, but are highly regulated in a dynamic manner.
hyaluronan molecular mass is not constant in biological fluids or tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

hyaluronan in biological fluids and tissue is highly variable, and that the size of hyaluron fragments may provide a sensitive indicator of tissue status, and may be useful in the development of biomarkers for disease.
hyaluronan in biological fluids and in the extracellular matrix is a complex, highly regulated, and dynamic molecule that plays important roles in cell biology and physiology.
the average molecular mass of hyaluronans is higher in healthy tissue, and lower when inflammation is present.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are a number of situations in which the hyaluronan molecular mass is reduced and its size distribution is broadened, and that these changes are associated with tissue-remodelling and/or inflammatory responses.
there is a strong correlation between hyaluronan molecular mass, size distribution and tissue or fluid content.
hyaluronan in tissues is not a simple polymer of constant size, but rather a complex mixture of polymers with different sizes and different biological properties.
